declared.title: How to protect eyewitness memory against the misinformation effect: A meta-analysis of post-warning studies
declared.venue: Journal of Applied Research in Memory and Cognition

population: participants of 25 misinformation experiments with a later warning (155 effect sizes); countries not listed in the abstract

findings.text: Telling people afterwards that some of what they heard was false cuts the misinformation effect to less than half its size on average

support.sentence: Key findings were that (1) post-warnings are surprisingly effective, reducing the misinformation effect to less than half of its size on average.

findings.text: The warning helps misled answers without harming the accuracy of answers that were not misled

support.sentence: (3) The post-warning reduction in the misinformation effect reflects a specific increase in misled performance (relative to no warning), at negligible cost for control performance.

limits: the sentences describe the warning's effect: that misinformation biases reports is assumed by every study pooled, not estimated in the abstract
25 lab studies, mostly with videos or slide shows of staged events
